overview: This one-page file consists of a list-of-papers or cross-reference entry concerning proposed investment of Formosan capital in the Netherlands Indies. It records a 19 October 1936 despatch from Hoover in Hong Kong forwarding a South China Morning Post report of 17 October about special loans by the Bank of Formosa to Japanese merchants, farmers, and industrialists operating in Malaya and the Netherlands Indies, while directing researchers to decimal file 894.51/474 for the underlying material.

people.name: Hoover
people.role: U.S. diplomatic or consular officer reporting from Hong Kong; precise position not stated

subfiles.title: List of papers on Formosan capital investment in the Netherlands Indies
subfiles.about: An administrative entry records and cross-references a despatch about Bank of Formosa loans to Japanese commercial and agricultural interests in Malaya and the Netherlands Indies.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists a 19 October 1936 despatch from Hoover in Hong Kong concerning special loans by the Bank of Formosa to Japanese merchants, farmers, and industrialists in Malaya and the Netherlands Indies. The despatch reportedly forwarded a South China Morning Post item dated 17 October 1936. The entry directs the reader to file 894.51/474, indicating that the substantive despatch and enclosure were filed elsewhere.

interest: The sheet is useful chiefly as archival evidence linking this subject file to material filed elsewhere under 894.51/474. Its reference to Bank of Formosa financing shows how Japanese economic expansion into Southeast Asia could operate through colonial Taiwanese financial institutions and target merchants, farmers, and industrialists together. It also identifies a contemporary Hong Kong newspaper report that may preserve details absent from this surviving file.
